Description: RP are the resource used for research attempts.
Every research attempt costs exactly 1 RP.
Current baseline conversion is 5 IPC → 1 RP.
Unspent RP carry over between turns.
RP are assigned at the beginning of the player's turn alongside normal purchases.
Each assigned RP targets one eligible technology.
The targeted technology remains secret until resolution.
Available/committed RP are public while targets remain secret.
Research attempts resolve during Deployment.
Roll of 1 fails and the RP is lost.
A failed research target remains undisclosed.
Roll of 2–5 acquires the targeted technology and consumes the RP.
Roll of 6 acquires the technology while retaining the RP.
Retained RP becomes available only in the following round.
Multiple RP may be assigned to different eligible technologies in one turn.
A technology must be eligible before it can be selected.
Dependencies determine research eligibility.
Alternatives within a dependency group are OR requirements.
Separate dependency groups are combined as AND requirements.
Eligibility is evaluated at turn start and remains fixed for that turn's assignments.
Newly acquired technology cannot create additional eligibility for already-assigned attempts.
A Research Centre may be required for specific technologies.
Facilities other than Research Centres do not themselves function as tech prerequisites.
Possession of a physical facility normally does not replace its technology dependency.
National restrictions may form part of eligibility.
Module-specific eligibility may apply when enabled.
Resources may form explicit prerequisites/payment requirements.
Order of checking prerequisites, RCENTER, nation, module and resources is not yet formalised.
Successful research acquires the technology.
Each technology has individually defined effects.
A technology may unlock construction/purchase of a facility or base.
A technology may unlock a unit or unit capability.
Unlocking an object does not automatically provide it unless explicitly stated.
Technology may modify an existing capability.
Technology may provide recurring or one-time bonuses.
Follow-up technologies normally depend on the unlocking technology rather than physical facility possession.
Technology has a primary domain.
Paths represent analytical routes and are not inherently mutually exclusive research programmes.
Technology definitions remain separate from physical object definitions.
Facilities and bases are physical game pieces on the map.
Facility types have individually defined functions.
Research Facilities are physical infrastructure.
Bases are physical military installations with defined operational effects.
Research Centres use the `RCENTER` classification.
A Research Centre may gate specific technologies.
Technology may unlock ability to build/purchase a facility.
Unlocking does not automatically place the facility.
Unlock, purchase/construction, placement and operation are separate events.
Facility effects are individually defined.
Facilities may receive applicable damage.
Damage can reduce/disable facility capabilities.
Damage/disablement does not remove researched technology.
Facilities belong to their territory and follow ownership/capture rules.
Facilities do not inherently generate RP.
RCENTER may generate RP or other research effects when explicitly defined.
Each facility has its own build/purchase cost.
Facility cost and research cost are separate.
Facility cost may reflect strategic capability.
A facility is represented as a physical object, not a duplicate technology node.
At most one facility of each type may occupy a territory.
Facilities may be strategically bombed; Bases may be tactically or strategically bombed.
Base is inoperative at 3+ damage; abilities return as repaired.
Purchasing a Research Centre immediately unlocks applicable Tier 4+ technologies and gives its establishment bonus.
Each Research Centre has an individually defined one-time establishment bonus.
The actual bonus and eligible “minor unit” must be defined per facility.
Unit attributes are maintained separately from technology definitions.
Special unit abilities are individually defined.
Special units otherwise follow normal A&A rules unless modified by their own rule.
Cost, attack, defence, movement, capacity and piece availability are data parameters.
RCENTER may provide a free unit when explicitly specified.
“Minor unit” in RCENTER bonuses requires an explicit definition/mapping.
Facilities can receive damage from applicable game effects.
Damage affects operation according to individual facility rules.
Damage does not remove technology.
Bases are inoperative at 3+ damage.
Repair restores damaged/inoperative capabilities according to applicable rules.
Repair costs, thresholds and effects are object-specific parameters.
Facilities are subject to territory ownership/capture.
Capturing a facility does not transfer researched technologies.
Losing a facility does not remove its technology.
Captured facilities operate according to their applicable rules.
Effect of capturing RCENTER on research eligibility must be defined.
Operation of specialised captured facilities without the associated technology requires explicit treatment where applicable.
Research assignments occur at the defined start-of-turn/Purchase & Repair point.
Eligibility uses the start-of-turn state.
Research resolves during Deployment.
Breakthrough RP cannot be reused during the current turn.
Individual technology/object effects occur at their specified game phase.
A consolidated timing reference is needed because R&D effects interact with several game phases.
Resources are represented separately from technologies.
Resource production may be tied to specific territories/sea zones.
Territory/sea-zone control can affect resource availability.
Resources may be nationally accessible without physical transportation.
Production may require physical infrastructure.
Basic resource infrastructure does not inherently require R&D.
R&D may improve resource infrastructure/production.
Optional resource modules may progress from geography → infrastructure → production → operational use → technological enhancement.
Locations, production rates, infrastructure and costs are maintained as data.
Oil is an abstract national resource and does not require physical transportation.
Oil production is geographically located and territorial control can affect supply.
Oil locations may be naturally active or require infrastructure.
Land and offshore extraction may use different infrastructure.
Oil Derrick is physical extraction infrastructure.
Oil Platform is physical offshore extraction infrastructure.
Synthetic Oil Plant provides synthetic oil production.
Oil production is collected during Income.
Oil has a defined storage limit/soft-cap mechanic.
Defined military operations consume Oil.
Oil shortage imposes defined operational penalties.
Bombing/damage can disable Oil infrastructure.
Convoys can affect Oil availability.
Required Oil may be substituted with IPC at the defined rate.
Oil Platforms can be captured through control of their sea zone.
Production, costs, storage, consumption and substitution values are data parameters.
Source: Oil Module / Tech List / Resource Territories

Description: Reactor Theory unlocks Nuclear Power Plant construction.
Nuclear Power Plant produces +1 IPC/turn.
Uranium Processing unlocks Nuclear Reactor construction.
Nuclear Reactor increases an NPP in the same territory to 2 IPC/turn.
Nuclear Reactor is a physical facility, not a technology node.
P.7.NU gives a Nuclear Reactor uranium-production capability.
P.8.NU gives the Nuclear Reactor Atomic Bomb production capability.
Atomic Bomb production consumes 2 Heavy Water + 1 Uranium.
Nuclear Submarines use nuclear propulsion.
Ballistic Missile Submarine is a distinct nuclear delivery capability.
Ballistic Missile Submarines can deliver Atomic Bombs.
Nuclear weapon delivery requires a qualifying delivery system.
Final Atomic Bomb delivery/drop procedure requires consolidated rule text.
P.9.NU currently functions as a placeholder rather than an ordinary research technology.
Nuclear rules should be checked against `XP GOING NUCLEAR v3`.
R&D consists of independent modules that can be added, removed or expanded without breaking the core.
Optional modules can add technologies, facilities, resources and effects.
Core R&D remains playable without optional modules.
Module-specific rules apply only when the module is enabled.
Exact configuration/activation procedure needs documentation.
Core R&D rules apply to both Global 1940 and Global Halifax.
Zombie system is an optional module.
AAZ is the mechanical baseline, adapted for Global.
Global uses an adapted Zombie deck.
Core AAZ mechanics remain while event variety expands.
Randomness primarily comes from cards and game-state effects.
Zombie events should interact with meaningful Global map/game conditions.
Existing R&D technologies may provide contextual Zombie benefits.
Dedicated Zombie technology remains limited and complementary to the main tree.
Zombie events, Desperate Measures, R&D and dedicated Zombie research may interact.
Relationship between Desperate Measures and R&D remains unresolved.
